- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot after sharp price spikes in history.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after recent highs and underestimates after recent lows.
- Forecast horizon 1–3 days shows significant lag; model reacts too slowly to recent price drops or spikes.
- When history includes a recent sharp decline, model fails to adjust downward quickly — underestimates the drop.
- Model overreacts to minor price volatility, especially in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 10–20).
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the final 5–10 days, often ignoring long-term downward trends or policy impacts.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or event-driven corrections — e.g., after policy changes or market interventions, forecasts remain unchanged.
